### If this adds or changes an ACT rule

- [ ] All passing examples from `corpus/act/testcases/<actId>/` are in the fixture set
- [ ] All failing examples are in the fixture set
- [ ] All inapplicable examples are in the fixture set
- [ ] At least two negative cases of my own: markup that resembles a violation and is not one
- [ ] `requires` declares every capability the rule actually needs. A rule that reads a computed style or a bounding box requires `layout`
- [ ] Measured accuracy pasted below, produced by `pnpm calibrate --rule <actId>` rather than estimated

<!-- Paste the calibrate output here. A poor number is fine and gets published as it is.
     A missing number is not, because then the table would contain an assertion. -->

### If this changes an engine mapping

- [ ] `kind` is honest: `exact`, `partial`, or `superset`
- [ ] The test case evidence is in this description
- [ ] The mapping test passes, which it will not if the corpus contradicts the claim

### If this changes a published number

- [ ] `calibration/table.json` was regenerated by the harness, not edited
- [ ] The diff in the table is explained above, per rule
- [ ] If any number got worse, that is stated plainly rather than buried

### If this changes the repair layer

- [ ] Idempotent: re-running on repaired source produces an empty edit list
- [ ] Deterministic: same input, same edits, same order
- [ ] Minimal: the union of edited ranges contains no byte outside an accessibility-relevant construct
- [ ] Property tests cover the above rather than examples

### If this touches a visual surface

- [ ] Screenshots at mobile and desktop widths, below
- [ ] Empty, loading, error, and dense-data states shown
- [ ] Marlo's own accessibility self-audit passes at WCAG 2.2 AA with zero critical or serious
- [ ] Keyboard complete, focus visible, reduced motion respected
- [ ] No meaning conveyed by colour alone

### If this needs a decision that is not mine to make

Leave this as a draft with the decisions listed here. Do not guess and do not merge.
